item.message: Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the 2% skills context budget. Codex can still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

item.text: {"brief_complete":false,"completion_reason":"Material workflow-experience decisions remain for Work entry, Coding review handoff, and Models operational hierarchy.","questions":[{"decision_key":"work_tab_entry_experience","label":"Work entry experience","context":"A conversation library is the searchable list of Chat, Coding, and Research conversations; reopening one restores only that conversation’s canonical context and memory.","evidence":"`apps/web/app/page.jsx` currently has no Work tab, while the approved six-tab design adds Work with three conversation modes. `packages/contracts/index.mjs` already defines per-run context, and the brief locks memory isolation per conversation, but neither source determines what operators see when entering Work.","impact":"This sets Work’s primary information hierarchy and whether returning operators prioritize continuity or starting new work. Long term, it determines how well large conversation histories remain navigable without exposing internal routing state.","question":"What should the Work tab show first when an operator opens it?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Conversation library","consequence":"Show recent conversations, search/filter, and a prominent New Conversation control; reopening is explicit, which adds one click but scales safely as history grows."},{"number":2,"text":"Resume last conversation","consequence":"Open the most recently active conversation immediately with history in a sidebar; this is fastest for continuity but can place an operator into stale or sensitive context unexpectedly."},{"number":3,"text":"New conversation composer","consequence":"Always open a blank Chat, Coding, or Research composer with history secondary; this makes starting work fastest but weakens resumability and encourages fragmented conversations."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"A library-first entry makes isolated conversation memory understandable, supports deliberate resumption, and remains usable as each operator accumulates many conversations.","priority":89},{"decision_key":"coding_result_review_handoff","label":"Coding review handoff","context":"A SimSpace is a content-hashed copy where coding work runs without modifying the source workspace; promotion is the separate command that applies an approved, validated result to that source.","evidence":"`docs/13-HARNESS-EXPERIMENTS.md` requires Coding work in a SimSpace followed by validation, approval, and separate promotion. `services/nexus-node/src/run-coordinator.mjs` already returns canonical results and artifact records, while the six-tab contract assigns immutable evidence and approvals to Runs.","impact":"This decides how Coding remains understandable without duplicating Runs. It directly affects review speed now and preserves a clear long-term ownership boundary for diffs, validation evidence, approval, and promotion.","question":"After a Coding run finishes validation, how should the operator review and advance its result?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Work summary, Runs review","consequence":"Show a concise diff and validation summary in Work, then open the authoritative review, approval, and promotion package in Runs; this preserves tab ownership with one deliberate handoff."},{"number":2,"text":"Full review inside Work","consequence":"Embed complete diffs, evidence, approval, and promotion controls in the conversation; this is convenient but duplicates Runs behavior and risks inconsistent authority surfaces."},{"number":3,"text":"Automatic switch to Runs","consequence":"Move the operator directly to the completed run’s review page; this avoids duplication but interrupts conversation flow and can feel disorienting during parallel work."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"A concise Work outcome preserves conversational continuity while keeping immutable evidence and consequential approval actions in the tab explicitly responsible for them.","priority":94},{"decision_key":"models_tab_primary_surface","label":"Models first screen","context":"Fleet health means whether each provider, runtime, and model is reachable, eligible for routing, loaded or warming, resource-constrained, or failing.","evidence":"`kits/providers-kit/index.mjs` owns provider profiles and health, `kits/routing-kit/index.mjs` owns eligibility and fallback rationale, and `docs/12-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` distinguishes live LM Studio proof from unproven cloud credentials. The existing Models surface in `apps/web/app/page.jsx` does not establish the hierarchy required for production operations.","impact":"This determines the Models tab’s hero controls and what an operator can diagnose without opening advanced panels. Long term, it shapes whether Models behaves primarily as an operations console, an installation catalog, or an analytics surface.","question":"What should dominate the first screen of the Models tab?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Fleet health and readiness","consequence":"Lead with eligible, loaded, warming, degraded, and failed resources plus essential load, unload, and retry actions; discovery and benchmarks remain advanced, favoring reliable operations."},{"number":2,"text":"Model catalog and discovery","consequence":"Lead with available and installable models plus import/download actions; acquisition becomes easier, but live failures and routing readiness require another view."},{"number":3,"text":"Usage and benchmarks","consequence":"Lead with latency, throughput, cost, and quality comparisons; optimization becomes prominent, but basic lifecycle and failure recovery are less immediate."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"NexusCentral’s routing and persistent retry behavior depend on operators understanding real readiness first; catalog and benchmark tasks are important but less urgent than keeping accepted work executable.","priority":86}]}
